chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Abul Qasim al-Baghowi told us, saying: Ali (that is, Ibn al-Ja'd) told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, saying: Al-Walid ibn al-Ayzar ibn Hareeth told us, saying: I heard Abu Amr al-Shaybani say: Abdullah ibn Mas'ood told me, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family):
Indeed, the most beloved of deeds to God are prayer, kindness (or filial piety/generosity), and striving (jihad).

key_terms.الْبَرُّ: Kindness, piety, or generosity (often referring to filial piety or general goodness)

ai.seo_question: What are the three most beloved deeds to God according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Ali ibn al-Jadd and recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, establishes a triad of excellence comprising ritual worship (Salat), social ethics (Al-Barr), and spiritual struggle (Al-Jihad). In Shia scholarship, 'Al-Barr' is often interpreted broadly to include filial piety and general righteousness, linking internal devotion with external conduct. This classification underscores the holistic nature of Islamic practice, where ritual purity and social justice are equally beloved to God.
